City Council Meeting Policy:
cityofpasadena.net/CityCouncilMeetingPolicy
Para facilitar la participación del público en reuniones realizadas
únicamente por medios electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del
público de la siguiente manera:
1. Ya sea que participen en persona
o virtualmente en la reunión, los miembros del público pueden proporcionar
comentarios públicos enviando una tarjeta de orador antes del comienzo de
los comentarios públicos sobre ese tema, en la siguiente página web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más de un artículo del
orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario en línea (los
oradores sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso publicado
en la agenda y lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el Consejo
Municipal). Los comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el
Alcalde y el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.
2. Participación
en reuniones en persona :
Complete una tarjeta de orador en línea
en el
siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Después de enviar una
tarjeta de orador público, los miembros del público pueden asistir a la
reunión en persona al acudir a la Cámara del Concejo Municipal de Pasadena,
Sala S249 en el Ayuntamiento en la fecha y hora de inicio de la reunión
publicada.
Participación en la reunión virtua l: para los participantes
virtuales, puede asistir conectándose a la reunión mediante una computadora,
otro dispositivo electrónico o por teléfono. Revise la agenda para
identificar la hora de inicio publicada para la reunión y conéctese a la
reunión justo antes o al comienzo de la reunión.
Para
participar en los comentarios públicos sobre un tema y ser reconocido para
hablar, se requiere que el orador inicie sesión en la reunión con el mismo
nombre o
número de teléfono que se usó en el formulario de la Tarjeta de orador. Esto
permitirá que el personal de la Ciudad ubique y ascienda al orador a la
reunión
cuando sea el momento de su comentario público. Las llamadas telefónicas de
los
participantes a la reunión del Concejo Municipal se grabarán como parte de
la reunión del Concejo Municipal. Al permanecer en línea y hacer comentarios
públicos durante la reunión del Concejo Municipal por teléfono, usted acepta
que se
grabe su llamada
telefónica. A continuación se muestra la información de conectividad para la
participación virtual:
Computadora o
dispositivos electrónicos, únase a la reunión en:
cityofpasadena.net/cczoom
Marcación telefónica
únicamente: 1-669-900-6833, ID de reunión: 161 482 446
3. Línea de ayuda
con la tarjeta de orador : si un orador de comentario público
necesita ayuda para completar una tarjeta de orador, llame a la oficina del
secretario municipal al: (626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda se abrirá 30
minutos antes de la hora de inicio publicada de la reunión.
4. Los miembros
del público pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier extensión antes del
inicio de la reunión, a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La correspondencia se enviará al Concejo Municipal antes del inicio de la
reunión, se publicará en línea y formará parte del registro legislativo del
tema.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 20, 2023-5:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber
  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING

  The meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.
OPENING:  Mayor Gordo and President Richardson Bailey called the
  Special Joint meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Unified
  School District (PUSD) Board of Education to order at 5:35 p.m.
  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by PUSD Boardmember
  Fredericks.

ROLL CALL:
  Councilmembers:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Vice Mayor Felicia Williams
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

Pasadena Unified School  President Michelle Richardson Bailey
District, Board of Education  Vice President Kimberly Kenne
  Boardmember Patrick Cahalan
  Boardmember Tina Fredericks
  Boardmember Jennifer Hall Lee
  Boardmember Patrice Marshall McKenzie
  Boardmember Dr. Yarma Velazquez

  Staff:  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools
  Leslie Barnes, Ed.D., Chief Business Officer
  Elizabeth J. Blanco, Ed.D., Chief Academic Officer

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo and President Richardson Bailey recognized Blair
  Hair School Boys Varsity Basketball Team on their first CIF-
  Southern Section Division 5A Championship, and presented the
  coaches and players with commendations.

  UPDATE ON CITY OF PASADENA'S EARLY CHILDHOOD
  DEVELOPMENT POLICY*

Council Minutes  1  03/20/2023
   Dr. Vera Vignes, Chair of the Early Child Development & Early
  Learning Task Force, provided a Powerpoint presentation on the
  agenda item, and responded to questions.

  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools, stated that
  there has been productive discussions with Dr. Vignes, Michelle
  Garrett and others to ensure that funding sources are identified
  to conduct the Early Development Instrument (EDI)
  Assessment. He expressed his enthusiasm for the partnership
  as the group works to collaboratively to attract more families to
  PUSD.

  Boardmember Hall Lee spoke in support of the collaboration to
  reach new families, which is an important component for the
  future success of the School District.

  Boardmember McKenzie requested that the proposed effort be
  as user-friendly as possible, minimizing barriers and making
  sure information and services are available and accessible to the
  families most in need.

  Councilmember Hampton spoke on the needs of children in the
  age category of infant to 5 years of age, how to identify locate
  those children most in need in the City, including through the
  Pasadena Public Health Department, an opportunity for the City
  and PUSD to partner in providing daycare and preschool
  services to this age group, and the need to extend outreach
  related to the Welcome Baby Campaign program to include
  fertility clinics located in Pasadena.

  Dr. Vera Vignes mentioned that there will be a huge launch of
  Pasadena's Early Child Development and Early Learning
  Initiative in 2024.

  Councilmember Madison thanked Dr. Vignes and the Task
  Force members for their work, recognized Carla Hegwood,
  Office of the Young Child, and asked the City Manager to provide
  information on the Council Standing Committee that would have
  jurisdiction over the work related to the Task Force.

  Boardmember Cahalan provided information on the Governor's
  budget and mid-year cuts, and encouraged everyone to stay
  informed when the May revision incorporates changes to the
  state's early childhood funding positions.

L  Mayor Gordo expressed appreciation and thanks to Dr. Vignes
  and the Task Force members for their work and effort in getting
  the City to this point. He also thanked the School District for their
  partnership and spoke on the importance of the EDI data as a

  Council Minutes  2  03/20/2023
   way to ensure services are provided in a coordinated manner to
  support the infant to 5 age group, so that when they arrive on
  PUSD school steps, they are prepared to succeed.

  The following individuals provided comments on the agenda
  item:

  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident
  Olden Denham, Pasadena resident
  Adrians Bautista, representing Black Live Matter (BLM)
  Pasadena
  Jasmine Richards Abdullah, representing BLM
  Anonymous, Residence not stated

  Mayor Gordo emphasized that there is a lot of work to be done,
  with the primary goal to identify those children that are most in
  need of the support as they prepare to enter the School District.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  DISCUSSION REGARDING A CAREER TECHNICAL
  EDUCATION (CTE) PILOT PROGRAM AND PARTNERSHIP

  Michelle Garrett, Assistant to the City Manager, presented a
  Powerpoint presentation on the item, and responded to
  questions.

  Dr. Laura Ramirez, Assistant Superintendent & Vice President
  of Instruction at Pasadena City College, and Dr. Kristina Turley,
  Coordinator, College and Career Pathways Program for PUSD
  presented a Powerpoint presentation on the item, and
  responded to questions.

  Due to technical difficulties, the City Clerk read a statement from
  Dr. Morgan, representing Huntington Hospital: "Huntington is
  proud to be part of this work group, hluntington is essentially a
  small city and needs workers of all types. Yes. The obvious as
  physicians and nurses but we need cooks, engineers, painters,
  technicians of all types, environmental services, service
  workers, security officers, therapists, electricians, and even
  administrators. We love working with our City, educational and
  community partners to keep local citizens here working in our
  communities."

  Chris Hanna, Executive Secretary, LA/OC Building Trades
  Council, presented a Powerpoint presentation on the item, and
  responded to questions.

Council Minutes  3  03/20/2023
   Doug Kranwinkle and Cynthia Kurtz, Task Force members,
  briefly spoke on the efforts of the Task Force and expressed their
\~  support for the proposed pilot program and partnership, noting
  the positive impact it will have on the City's young people.

  Vice Mayor Williams briefly spoke on the San Gabriel Valley
  Economic Forecast that reported on the labor force and housing
  gap challenges in the region, and expressed her support for the
  CTE pilot program and partnership, as well as a community
  benefits program that connects the City's land use polices,
  building codes, etc., with the training/education to enable those
  living and learning in Pasadena to have the opportunity to also
  work in the City, and encouraged a robust outreach effort that
  will reach all constituents and PUSD students and parents.

  Boardmember Velazquez, stated: "the Pasadena public
  education system also trains and will train the leaders of all of
  these institutions. We will train the nurses, but we will also train
  the chief surgeons and chief doctors of this community. And so
  it is our responsibility to provide students with the choices that
  they want for their education, and I am particularly happy with
  the opportunity to bring new commerce and new students with
  more opportunities to their development in the City and in this
  state. But it is not because we are a public education system that
  serves predominantly diverse students that we are a good fit for
  this type of initiative. It is because we are an education system
  that is committed to the success of all of their students
  regardless of their choices."

  Boardmember Hall Lee advocated for humanities to be part of
  the trade school education/program, stating it is essential to the
  pursuit of happiness.

  Dr. Morgan reiterated her comments that were read out loud by
  the City Clerk, and expressed it is Huntington Hospital's hope to
  contribute to this effort, increasing opportunities for local
  students and enable Pasadena residents the opportunity to
  continue to live and work in Pasadena.

  Boardmember Fredericks expressed her support for the
  program and partnership with the City, and requested that staff
  track and chart the progress participants.

  Boardmember McKenzie expressed her support for the
  proposal, highlighted the incredible opportunity that is on the
L  horizon with the upcoming 2028 Olympics games to be held in
  Los Angeles, and noted the need to train and provide a
  workforce able to meet timelines and deliverables for the
  Olympics.

  Council Minutes  4  03/20/2023
   The following individuals provided comments on the item:

  Adriana Bautista, representing BLM Pasadena
  Jasmine Richards Abdullah, representing BLM
  Pasadena
  Anne-Marie Otey, representing LA/OC Counties
  Building Trades
  Alien Shay, Pasadena resident
  Marlene Benites, Pasadena resident
  Anonymous, Residence not stated

  Mayor Gordo stated that he believes there is an opportunity to
  refurbish one of the PUSD school sites to meet the needs of
  these programs and asked that this be a central point for future
  discussions once formal action is taken.

  Assistant City Manager Reyes noted that City staff, at the
  direction of the City Manager, has applied for a federal grant that
  would allow for either the construction and/or rehabilitation of an
  existing building for the purpose of providing needed space for
  such programs, and stated the City also intends to pursue
  available state grants in partnership with PUSD.

  President Richardson Bailey expressed excitement for this
  partnership, and mentioned Twilight Adult Education Franklin
  Site as a potential location.

  Boardmember Cahalan echoed Presidents Richardson Bailey's
  comments and provided information on the process for school
  construction and modernization projects, noting that approval by
  the Division of the State Architect (DSA) may take up to a year
  if plans are not received by the end of April, or beginning of May.

  In response to Councilmember Madison's comments, Mayor
  Gordo stated the action today is to formalize the partnership and
  allow staff from the City and PUSD to proceed in pursuing
  funding, with direction to the Superintendent, City Attorney, and
  the City Manager to come back to City Council with any
  additional actions to formalize the approval.

  Councilmember Hampton thanked the public speakers for their
  comments, stating that the City Council is committed to figuring
  out a path for success for everyone. He expressed he will
  advocate for eliminating barrier, highlighting the first sentence of
  the vision statement that states, "Everyone deserves a path to
L  success", which also includes individuals with disabilities,
  students with IEP'S, etc., and commented that once the
  partnership is formed, he would like to see all the public
  speakers who came out tonight at the table.

  Council Minutes  5  03/20/2023
   Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember
  Hampton, seconded by Councilmember Jones, to formalize the
\~  partnership with the Pasadena Unified School District and
  Pasadena City College to create a Career Technical Education
  (CTE) Pilot Program and Partnership, and to authorize City staff
  to work with PUSD in pursuing federal and state funding
  opportunities:

  AYES: Councilmembers Hampton, Jones, Lyon, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Vice Mayor Williams, Mayor Gordo
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  It was moved by Boardmember McKenzie, seconded by
  Boardmember Hall Lee to formalize the partnerships with the
  City of Pasadena and Pasadena City College to create a Career
  Technical Education (CTE) Pilot Program and Partnership, and
  to authorize PUSD staff to work with the City in pursuing federal
  and state funding opportunities

  AYES: Boardmember Cahalan, Fredericks, Hall Lee,
  McKenzie, Velazquez, Vice President Kenne,
  President Richardson Bailey
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  UPDATE ON THE PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL
  DISTRICT'S FACILITIES MASTER PLAN

  Leslie Barnes, Ed.D. Chief Business Officers, presented an oral
  presentation on the item, and responded to questions.

  Discussion occurred and touched on matters related to the
  condition of school grounds, maintenance schedule for school
  sites (whether in-use or not in-use), and bond/measure funding
  available to address maintenance issues. It was requested that
  future joint meeting topics include information regarding vacant
  properties, plans for school sites, and how the City can support
  the School District, including the potential of forming a working
  group comprised of City and School District members, to
  address these matters going forward.

  President Richardson Bailey suggested that there may be an
  opportunity for the City Council to participate as a liaison for the
  City at PUSD Facilities Committee, but stating this is just one of
  the Board's Committees, and is open to further discussion on
  how to work with the City on this issue.

  Council Minutes  6  03/20/2023
   Mayor Gordo cited the 710 Working Group as one example
  where the City Council appointed a member of the School Board
r  to include that perspective as part of that body, suggesting that
  perhaps a Councilmember can participate in the formal
  discussions surrounding the future of school sites, and
  requested that the City Manager, City Attorney, and/or
  Superintendent provide some advice on how such a similar
  arrangement may be achieved on the part of the School Board.

  Councilmember Madison spoke on state legislation that is very
  supportive of educator workforce housing, noting the potential
  for opportunities for workforce housing as part of the 710
  relinquishment property discussion.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that nine letters expressing
  concerns with the condition of the Allendale Elementary School
  campus; six letters expressing concerns with the condition of the
  Linda Vista Elementary School site; 1 letter expressing general
  concerns with the condition of school grounds in Pasadena; and
  all letters providing suggestions and recommendations to
  improve the maintenance and upkeep of school sites; and one
  letter expressing concerns with the School Board not using
  Measure 0 funding for public charter schools, were received by
  the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council and Board
  of Education, posted online, and made part of the public record
  for the item.

  The following individuals provided comments on the matter:

  Rene Gonzalez, Pasadena resident
  Julieta Aragon, Pasadena resident
  Diane Kirby, Pasadena resident
  John Penido, Pasadena resident
  Ken Kiessling, representing Linda Vista Annandale
  Association
  Jeff Bulgin, Pasadena resident
  Jessica Bulgin, Pasadena resident
  Nina Chomsky, representing Linda Vista Annandale
  Association
  George Barajas, Pasadena resident
  Brent Sorenson, Pasadena resident
  Amy Valencia, Pasadena resident
  Anonymous, Residence not stated
  Jill Shook, representing Making Housing and Community
  Happen
  Lindsay Amstutz, Pasadena resident
  Paul Holliday, representing Linda Vista Children's Center

  Council Minutes  7  03/20/2023
   In response to comments regarding the walkway behind Field
  Elementary School, Assistant City Manager Reyes stated that
r  City and PUSD staff are looking at the situation with the Public
  Works Director to understand where the City and School District
  stands on this matter.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the concerns expressed by the public
  speakers related to the Linda Vista school site and stated the
  City's readiness to assist the School District with addressing the
  maintenance concerns, such as by possible utilizing the City's
  MASH Program to provide maintenance and upkeep, while
  acknowledging that PUSD does have existing contracts with
  teamsters, and this would have to be looked into further.

  Dr. Brian McDonald, Superintendent of Schools, provided
  information on the walkway located adjacent to Field Elementary
  School, stating that after the Uvalde school shooting, the District
  became aware of the access to the school through the walkway.
  Giving careful consideration, as well as legal advice, the School
  District reinstalled the gate for security reasons. He noted that a
  compromise may be possible by designing a fence that would
  allow resident access to the walkway. In regard to the Linda
  Vista school site, the Superintendent stated that the School
  District will look at addressing the issue as soon as possible.

  In relation to the Field Elementary School walkway, Leslie
  Barnes, Ed.D. Chief Business Officer, stated that as soon as the
  Division of State Architects signs off on the drawings, PUSD will
  host a community meeting on next steps.

  Mayor Gordo asked the Boardmembers to keep the City Council
  updated on matters pertaining to Field Elementary, Linda Vista
  Elementary, and Annandale Elementary sites.

  Boardmember Velazquez stated that the Superintendent's
  Office and the Facilities Office have been incredibly responsive
  to all of her inquiries with regards to Linda Vista Elementary site,
  allowing for active communication with neighbors; and noting
  she is in the process of creating an advisory committee to
  discuss these issues and thanked the neighbors for their
  participation at tonight's meeting.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  UPDATE ON PASADENA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT'S
  OVERALL FISCAL OUTLOOK, INCLUDING

  A. REPORT ON THE USE OF MEASURE I FUNDS

  Council Minutes  8  03/20/2023
   B. REPORT ON THE EXPIRATION OF THE STATE'S "HOLD
  HARMLESS" PROVISIONS RELATED TO AVERAGE DAILY
[  ATTENDANCE (ADA)

  Leslie Barnes, Ed. D. Chief Business Officers, presented a
  Powerpoint presentation on the item, and responded to
  questions.

  Elizabeth J. Blanco, Ed.D., Chief Academic Officer responded to
  questions regarding the School District's "signature" programs,
  declining enrollment, and the educational master plan.

  Boardmember Hall Lee briefly spoke on new regulations related
  to enrollment versus Average Daily Attendance (ADA) to point
  out the issue's high complexity, and spoke on the importance of
  signature programs.

  Boardmember Kenne advocated for the School District to utilize
  Measure J funds for signature programs as opposed to the
  current practice of using supplemental and concentration grant
  funds, which are intended to support low income, English
  learner, foster youth, and career technical education. She stated
  her support to set aside funds for maintenance issues.

  Councilmember Madison requested a copy of the Powerpoint
  presentation.

  Rene Gonzalez, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns
  with PUSD's fiscal health, noting that teachers' salaries are
  not competitive; and advocated for increasing School
  District revenues, as well as potentially monitoring
  overspending through a Board sub-committee.

  Following discussion, on order of the President and Mayor, and
  by consensus, the information was received and filed.

  ANNOUNCEMENT OF SCIENCE FEST 2023 AT MUIR HIGH
  SCHOOL ON APRIL 22, 2023 AND EARTH DAY

  Vice Mayor Williams provided information on Science Fest 2023
  at Muir High School, thanked Warren Skidmore and other lead
  organizers for inviting the City to participate, and thanked City
  Manager Marquez and Assistant City Manager Reyes for
  organizing the participation of various City departments.

  Boardmember Hall Lee announced PUSD's 2023 Women's
  hlistory Month event, "My Body, My Choice, Our Rights", which
  includes Dolores Huerta and a pre-recorded keynote address by
  Byllye Avery on March 22, 2023 from 6:00 - 7:30 p.m.

  Council Minutes  9  03/20/2023
   Councilmember Hampton expressed appreciation and gratitude
  to the PUSD Board of Education for participating in a productive
r  meeting, and shared that he and Vice Mayor Williams attended
  an Aviation conference at the Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena
  Airport, and that he is working to connect PUSD with the Airport
  Authority to discuss job opportunities and potential areas for
  collaboration.

  ADJOURNMENT  On the order of the President and Mayor, the special joint
  meeting of the City Council and Pasadena Board of Education
  adjourned at 10:13 p.m.
